Introduction

This document outlines the equipment inspection I1, which must be performed 
 on an annually bases as 
indicated by Y1 in the title block.

The first
draft is initiated by eng. Ekramy Mostafa Mohamad, tested by eng Gamal Abdel Meniem Abu Saree, accepted by general 
 director of mechanical maintenance eng. Ebrahim Zarea and approved by eng. Fathi El Sayed head 
 sector of Kurimat PS. This document 
 certified by eng. Gamal El-Din Abdel Wahab UEEPC general director of
 inspection & quality control and MPIS Coordinator.
Safety Precautions

items:
A work permit must be issued and the qualified maintenance 
 staff should carry the suitable safety category.

Maintenance staff should be will trained and qualified or directly supervised 
 by some one who is.

Safety fence with caution marks surrounding the work area 
 is required.

Wear your 
 safety and healthy equipment as safety helmet, safety shoes, breathing mask, 
 safety glass ...etc
Isolate the circuit breaker for the Seal Air Fan.

Maintenance Procedures

a) 
 Disassemble the coupling and inspect for wear.

b) 
Replace worn parts.
c) Clean grease from coupling and repack with new grease.
Periodic Lubrication

The required frequency of 
lubrication is directly related to the type of lubricant chosen, and the 
operating conditions.

Steelflex couplings lubricated with common industrial
lubricants should be relubed annually.

The use of Falk Long Term Grease
(LTG) will allow relube intervals to be extended to
beyond five years.

When relubing,
remove both lube plugs and insert lube fitting.

Fill with recommended lubricant
until an excess appears at the opposite hole.

Caution: Make certain all plugs have been inserted after
lubricating.

Bearing

Disassembly of the Renk 
Sleeve Bearing System Pedestal type "ER" - Finned Housing (with type 10 Seal On 
Both Sides)

To disassemble the bearing liner and
all associated parts from the bearing housing, carry out the following
instructions. Carefully store all disassembled parts in a safe location.

Thoroughly
clean the exterior of the bearing housing. Loosen and remove the oil drain plug
(1) at the bottom of the bearing housing (2). Drain the oil from the bearing
housing.

Loosen and remove the bolts (6) at
the split line of the bearing housing (2) and bearing housing 
cap (5).

Use the lifting eyebolts (10) to lift (by hand or hoist) the bearing housing
cap (5) straight up, so that the cap is completely disengaged from the lower
halves of the labyrinth seals (18), labyrinth seal carriers (13), bearing
housing (2), and the bearing liner (16).

Pull the bearing housing cap (5) forward out of and away from the bearing area.
Loosen and remove the bolts (14) securing the upper halves of the seal carriers
(13) to the bearing housing cap (5). Remove the seal carriers.

Lift (by hand
or hoist) the upper half of the bearing liner (15) and remove it.

Loosen and remove the bolts at the
split line of the oil ring (17). Carefully disengage the dowels holding the oil
ring halves together and remove the oil ring.

Remove the garter springs (19) that encircle the labyrinth seals (18). Lift off
the upper half of each seal, then rotate the lower half of each seal out of the groove in
the lower half of each seal carrier (13).

Disconnect and
remove RTD's, thermocouples, or any other temperature
detecting instruments that enter the lower half of the bearing liner (16).

Using a hoist
or jack, raise the shaft slightly so that the lower half of the bearing liner
(16) can be rolled out of the bearing housing (2).

Roll out (be careful not to use
excessive force) the lower half of the bearing liner (16) and 
remove it.

Loosen and remove the bolts (14)
securing the lower halves of the seal carriers (13) to the bearing housing (2).
Remove the seal carriers.

Thoroughly clean and inspect all individual parts which have been removed.
Clean the interior of the bearing housing.
To reassemble the Renk Bearing System, follow the preceding instructions in the reverse order.

sections.text: Disassembly Instructions
Reassembly

Check
mounting structure, making sure it is rigid, level and well supported.

Inspect shaft to ensure it is smooth (Ra ≤ 0.4,
equivalent to 32 micro-inch finish, or better), within the dimensions and
tolerances given by RENK Corporation and free of burrs or rough spots.

After removing the upper part of the housing (2) and the
bearing liner (3 & 4), the interior of the housing and the remaining surfaces
of the liner are to be cleaned thoroughly and checked for any damage caused in
transit.

Before the bottom liner half 
is
replaced, apply oil to the spherical seats in the housing base and the liner.
The shaft (5) may now be partially lowered into position. Special care must be
taken so that the axial surfaces of the locating bearing are not damaged.

As soon as the shaft has reached a distance of approx. 2
mm (0.08 Inch) from the liner base, the housing base can be precisely aligned.
The control is made by checking the distances between the shaft and the lateral
bores in the housing.

After the split faces of the bottom liner half and the
housing base are aligned, apply oil to the shaft
and the liner. Then lower the shaft into place in the liner. With a slight
hammer blow against the housing base settle the liner into its seating so that
the liner axis and shaft axis are parallel.

The loose oil
ring (6) is installed next.

The ring must be handled with special
care as reliable operation of the bearing is also dependent on the effective and reliable
functioning of the oil ring.
The bolts must be tightly fastened.

Split
misalignment must be avoided and any burrs or edges carefully removed in order
to ensure smooth running of the ring.

In
any dis- and reassembly, care must be taken that the
oil ring is not distorted and its geometrical shape is maintained.

The outside of the two liner halves is stamped with
identification numbers or marks near the split line.

Make
sure that these marks align and the split faces are clean when placing-the top
liner half (3) Into position.

Incorrect fitting may lead to heavy damage due to clamping
of the shaft.

Check
to ensure that the loose oil ring can still rotate freely on the shaft.

After coating the housing
split faces with a non hardening sealing compound, place the housing cap (3)
into position.

Care
must be taken that the identification numbers or marks match.

Ensure
also that the anti rotation pin is seated without any contact to the
corresponding hole in the liner.

The cap bolts (7) must be tightened diagonally and
securely to prevent any loss of oil through the split line of any loosening of
the housing in cases where the installation is subject to vibration.

sections.text: Oil Filling

The bearing can be filled with the prescribed type of oil
through the hole for the top sight glass (8) or through a thermometer hole (1).

All
holes and threads not used are to be closed by pipe plugs. Also check all
connections for oil leaks.

Filling
the bearing with lubricant beyond the middle of the oil sight glass (11) does
not impair the function of the bearing, but there is a possibility that excess
oil may leak out
through the shaft seals.

Disassembly Instructions

Reassembly
Check
mounting structure, making sure it is rigid, level and well supported.
Inspect shaft to ensure it is smooth (Ra ≤ 0.4,
equivalent to 32 micro-inch finish, or better), within the dimensions and
tolerances given by RENK Corporation and free of burrs or rough spots.
After removing the upper part of the housing (2) and the
bearing liner (3 & 4), the interior of the housing and the remaining surfaces
of the liner are to be cleaned thoroughly and checked for any damage caused in
transit.
Before the bottom liner half 
is
replaced, apply oil to the spherical seats in the housing base and the liner.
The shaft (5) may now be partially lowered into position. Special care must be
taken so that the axial surfaces of the locating bearing are not damaged.
As soon as the shaft has reached a distance of approx. 2
mm (0.08 Inch) from the liner base, the housing base can be precisely aligned.
The control is made by checking the distances between the shaft and the lateral
bores in the housing.
After the split faces of the bottom liner half and the
housing base are aligned, apply oil to the shaft
and the liner. Then lower the shaft into place in the liner. With a slight
hammer blow against the housing base settle the liner into its seating so that
the liner axis and shaft axis are parallel.
The loose oil
ring (6) is installed next.
The ring must be handled with special
care as reliable operation of the bearing is also dependent on the effective and reliable
functioning of the oil ring.
The bolts must be tightly fastened.
Split
misalignment must be avoided and any burrs or edges carefully removed in order
to ensure smooth running of the ring.
In
any dis- and reassembly, care must be taken that the
oil ring is not distorted and its geometrical shape is maintained.
The outside of the two liner halves is stamped with
identification numbers or marks near the split line.
Make
sure that these marks align and the split faces are clean when placing-the top
liner half (3) Into position.
Incorrect fitting may lead to heavy damage due to clamping
of the shaft.
Check
to ensure that the loose oil ring can still rotate freely on the shaft.
After coating the housing
split faces with a non hardening sealing compound, place the housing cap (3)
into position.
Care
must be taken that the identification numbers or marks match.
Ensure
also that the anti rotation pin is seated without any contact to the
corresponding hole in the liner.
The cap bolts (7) must be tightened diagonally and
securely to prevent any loss of oil through the split line of any loosening of
the housing in cases where the installation is subject to vibration.

Oil Filling
The bearing can be filled with the prescribed type of oil
through the hole for the top sight glass (8) or through a thermometer hole (1).
All
holes and threads not used are to be closed by pipe plugs. Also check all
connections for oil leaks.
Filling
the bearing with lubricant beyond the middle of the oil sight glass (11) does
not impair the function of the bearing, but there is a possibility that excess
oil may leak out
through the shaft seals.
